title: When not to invent a collection (use the BCL)
hook: The Base Class Library (BCL) already has the pipe, the set, and the list. Writing a custom AsyncQueue in a worker is usually Channel<T> with extra bugs — name the right type and move on.

blocks.text: Before you write a custom collection class, check whether the BCL already solves your problem. Need a growable buffer? List<T>. Need lookup? Dictionary<TKey, TValue> or FrozenDictionary after startup. Need uniqueness? HashSet<T>. Need a snapshot many readers share? ImmutableArray or ImmutableDictionary. Need a bounded in-memory pipe between async methods? Channel<T> in System.Threading.Channels. Custom collections are justified when you have a domain-specific invariant — not because you wanted a class named MessageBag.

entries.plainDefinition: A thread-safe, bounded or unbounded pipe for passing items between producers and consumers inside one process.
A thread-safe dictionary from System.Collections.Concurrent for shared mutable maps under high concurrency.
A read-only dictionary from System.Collections.Immutable. Updates return a new copy; safe to share across threads.
An optimized read-only dictionary built at startup for maximum lookup speed.

blocks.text: Inventing a new collection type is a smell unless you can name the invariant List cannot express. A custom thread-safe list with public lock fields is reinventing ConcurrentBag badly. Exposing ConcurrentQueue as a substitute for SQS loses durability. Building a custom enumerator that hits Redis on every MoveNext hides latency and retries from the caller. Interviews test whether you know the standard library — not whether you can write a lock around Queue<T> from first principles.

blocks.title: Name the BCL type first
blocks.body: If asked how to coordinate producers in one process, say Channel<T>. If asked how to store tenant feature flags for a Lambda lifetime, say Dictionary or FrozenDictionary loaded at startup.

sections.heading: How to choose the right type

items.title: Is the data in one process?
items.body: Yes → BCL in-memory types. No → external store (Redis, SQS, database).

items.title: Do multiple threads write?
items.body: Yes → ConcurrentDictionary, Channel<T>, or a lock around a simple type. No → List, Dictionary, Queue are fine.

items.title: Is the data read-only after startup?
items.body: Yes → ImmutableArray, ImmutableDictionary, or FrozenDictionary for fast shared reads.

items.title: Is it a producer/consumer pipe?
items.body: Yes → Channel<T> with bounded capacity and backpressure. Full API in module 15.

diagram.title: BCL collection landscape

flowchart TD

  Need -->|Growable buffer| L[List T]
  Need -->|Key lookup| D[Dictionary or FrozenDictionary]
  Need -->|Uniqueness| H[HashSet T]
  Need -->|FIFO single thread| Q[Queue T]
  Need -->|Async producer consumer| C[Channel T module 15]
  Need -->|Thread-safe shared map| CD[ConcurrentDictionary]
  Need -->|Read-only snapshot| IM[ImmutableArray or ImmutableDictionary]
  Need -->|Distributed durable queue| SQS[SQS not a BCL type]

snippet.label: Name Channel, do not implement it
snippet.explanation: If data never leaves the process and producers are async, Channel<T> is the type. If you just accumulated one ReceiveMessage page, List is enough.

snippet.label: Do not disguise I/O as IEnumerable
snippet.explanation: Prefer an explicit client method that returns IReadOnlyList<T> or IAsyncEnumerable<T> (module 13) so the caller sees the I/O cost.

snippet.label: FrozenDictionary for startup config
snippet.explanation: Load once at startup, freeze for fast shared reads. No locks needed because nothing mutates after freezing.

blocks.text: Node.js has no built-in Channel or ConcurrentDictionary. Node streams and async iterators are the analogue of IAsyncEnumerable and Channel — not of Array.push in a loop. In TypeScript, you might reach for a library like p-queue for bounded concurrency; in C#, Channel<T> is in the standard library. The lesson is the same: do not reinvent a pipe when the runtime or standard library already ships one.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Writing a thread-safe list with public lock fields instead of using ConcurrentBag or Channel<T>. Exposing ConcurrentQueue as a substitute for SQS and losing durability. Building a custom enumerator that hits Redis on every MoveNext — hide I/O behind explicit methods.

interviewTakeaways: Prefer BCL generic collections; ArrayList and Hashtable are legacy.
Channel<T> is the in-process async queue — details in module 15.
Do not disguise I/O as IEnumerable unless the contract is explicitly a stream (module 13).
commonPitfalls: Writing a thread-safe list with public lock fields.
